bulk_mfa_reenrol.why: 500 mfa_disabled by a support service account in two hours: a policy migration

cgnat.why: hundreds of accounts behind one carrier egress address

dormant_returner.why: silent for 40-80 days, then back on the known device

duplicate_owner.why: one person with two accounts linked to the same provider identity

email_migrant.why: email change with MFA step-up and verification, from the known device

fake_account_farm.why: abuse, but not account takeover: no real owner existed before the farm

forced_reset.why: the store's own compromised-credential policy forced a reset after the wave

forgetful.why: several failures then a self-service reset, all from the known device

geo_glitch.why: the geo-IP provider mapped their block to Brazil for three days: fake impossible travel

gift_buyer.why: December orders shipped to other people in other countries

household.why: 2-4 accounts on one shared desktop for months: a legitimate graph hub

marketing_burst.why: 600 real signups in six hours after a promo email

new_phone.why: new device, fingerprint and TLS stack, same network and timezone, MFA passed

night_shift.why: habitual 02:00-05:00 local logins: a login-hour anomaly that is their normal

privacy_browser.why: fingerprint changes every session, cookies sometimes cleared: looks like device churn

pw_manager_migrant.why: password change, MFA enabled and passkey added within minutes, from the known device

qa_robot.why: automated smoke tests from a datacenter on a shared device, every few hours

relocator.why: permanent move: new country, new address, new phone number, and it stays that way

shared_access_couple.why: two people, two devices, different hours and locale on one account

spray_target.why: one failed attempt from the spraying wave; no takeover

stuffing_target.why: attacked and not taken over: the failures are the attacker's, the account is still the owner's

support_recovery.why: ticket, support reset, login; 40% from a new device because the old one is gone

traveller.why: new country on a known device; a quarter change their password on the trip

typical.why: home broadband, one or two devices, nothing unusual

vpn_always_on.why: datacenter ASN and a foreign country, every day, for months
